head_commit.message:
feat(pipeline): phase 3 — the quality generation depth (#969)

* feat(pipeline): phase 3 quality-depth rust spine + ipc contract

- pipeline/resume: flat serde artifact types w/ filled examples,
  stage prompts interpolating the generated prompt_blocks (no third
  copy), ADR-017 cache keys (PIPELINE_PROMPT_VERSION pinned), six
  stages behind Pipeline::run_hooked
- structurally model-proof: evidence quotes verbatim-filtered with
  status overwritten from the keywords kernel; strategy rebuilt on the
  seeded roster (model authors only angle/emphasis, never the roster,
  <=8 plans + condensed group); every Critical deterministic
- repair <=2 rounds, section-scoped splice, strictly-more-criticals
  reverts; unsourced_metric located via evidence span (label-only
  grouping left the commonest Critical unrepairable)
- commands/resume_pipeline: five commands, RunHooks as the sole
  emit/persist/stop point, v2 quality-report wrapper
- run_timeout re-derivation proved the Phase-2 flag right in the
  dangerous direction: 30 min < the 1800s the three JSON stages can
  legitimately consume; floor raised to 45 min, pinned both sides
  against quality_run_deadline; max_tokens documented as unenforced
- resumePipeline IPC contract + namespaces + mock-client wiring;
  qualityRunDeadlineSecs in ai-timeouts with renderer>backend lock
- 18/18 mutation battery (incl. one re-aimed after hitting dead code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(renderer): quality-report round-trip preserves depth + fabrications

- pipeline widened from the 'fast' literal to GenerationDepth; parse
  preserves the stored depth (unknown/missing -> 'fast' for v1 compat)
  instead of re-stamping
- parseSlot overlays the validated report onto the raw slot so
  fabrications and future pipeline-side keys survive the round-trip;
  fabrications stays deliberately untyped-opaque (typing without
  validating is the defect class the overlay avoids)
- mergeRecheckedReport had the SAME defect one layer down (rebuilt the
  slot from scratch) — a Re-check would still have wiped the review
  list and Remove/Keep verdicts after the parser fix; now overlays
- byte-level round-trip + end-to-end persisted-blob tests; 4/4
  mutations caught (re-stamp, dropped spread, dropped merge overlay,
  merged-wrapper re-stamp)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): close phase 3 critic round (19 findings)

- terminal_state derives status+reason together; cancel token consulted
  on the error path; a failed run can never report "done" (cancel
  mid-draft previously surfaced as failed+done -> renderer success)
- RunDeadline shared by hooks and repair loop: checked between rounds
  AND between per-section calls, stopping with RunTimeout keeping
  progress; deadline re-derived (fixed 1800->4200s, passes 3->1,
  budget floor 45->75 min) — repair calls are flat-bounded so they
  belong in the fixed term, not effort-scaled; both lock tests now
  compute inner bounds from the fan-out constants (the old TS test was
  an identity that could not fail)
- regenerate_section acquires the agent_run limiter (was the only
  provider-calling command with no admission)
- ensure_latest_run refuses non-latest runs (aggregate-row confusion);
  per-section repair error = failed attempt, RateLimited = Budgeted;
  strategy matches roles by name only + emphasis filtered against the
  grounded evidence map; artifacts compact-serialized with cap sized
  on MEASURED worst cases (16k; evidence artifact measured 13.2k vs
  the 3.9k estimate)
- server-side clamps hoisted from commands/resume.rs; normalized
  language token in the system slot; fence patterns match attribute
  form <tag x=..> for all 19 tags (empirically re-run hostile set)
- Completer seam extracted + 6 end-to-end repair-loop tests; the
  parse_resume lines 1:1 assumption pinned; stoppedReason widened to
  nullable in the contract (status is the authority)
- 21 mutations applied, all caught (2 initially survived — re-aimed)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(renderer): phase 3 quality-depth ui

- resume-pipeline machine + session hook: coarse run states, stage
  index/total/phase/attempt, cancel via jobs.cancel, reconnect via
  initialRunId; TERMINAL DETECTION READS RUN STATUS ONLY (a cancel or
  deadline stop emits no pipeline:stage event at all — before() errs
  ahead of its start emit; contract doc corrected) backed by a
  busy-gated poll; draft consumed via onStream, never awaitAiStream
- generation-store ADR-006 siblings (runId/pipelineStage/
  sectionStates); fast path asserted byte-identical
- depth selection: Settings default + per-run override in both
  wizards; per-option tooltips + info popover with honest cost table;
  max shown disabled with reason (backend rejects it this phase);
  soft small-model warning (never blocks)
- staged GeneratingPanel (StepDots from index/total, streamed draft
  display-only); section verdict chips; Fix-this-section ->
  regenerateSection surfacing the non-latest-run refusal honestly
- terminal Remove/Keep fabrication review with its own validating
  parser (the opaque carry is deliberate); entries whose evidence no
  longer occurs in the document render as "no longer in the document"
- per-job runs list (<=3, status/depth/date + report)
- en+de i18n (2352=2352 parity); 10/10 mutations caught (one re-aimed
  after a fixture tripped a sibling guard)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): close delta round 2 (retry budget, terminal matrix, fence)

- send_with_retry/send_stream_with_retry now OWN the per-request
  timeout as a total budget (retries get only the remainder — a
  sequence cannot outlive its bound); 14 call sites dropped their
  builder .timeout; the streaming twin's duplicated stream_deadline
  argument collapsed. QUALITY_RUN_FIXED_SECS 4200 is now correct
  rather than accidental; client margin 60->960s (worst in-flight
  overshoot is stream_deadline(max)); argued deviation: MAX_ATTEMPTS
  no longer bounds anything, so no test couples to it — the budget is
  the bound and IS mutation-pinned
- terminal_state takes persisted: a boundary RunTimeout with a saved
  document is needsReview/completed, and the job event moved with it
  (job_complete whenever status != failed)
- complete_json takes a required deadline guard composed into charge —
  the re-ask cannot fire past deadline; single source for the
  run-timeout message
- fence neutralizer writes the matched run BACK instead of dropping it
  (the executed proof showed 3 posting lines deleted); the reviewer's
  prescribed {0,200} bound was probed and REJECTED — padded attributes
  survive it; pattern stays unbounded+newline-tolerant, hostile set
  96 tests green; agent/tools.rs split at R8 (tests -> tools/test.rs)
- emphasisDropped count on the strategy artifact; repair timing test
  margins one-sided; is_verbatim cfg(test); ensure_latest_run message
  honest; TS lock notes the Rust twin is the live guard

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(ui): segmented-control support for the depth selector

Part of the phase 3 renderer build (belongs with 379272e2; missed by
path staging).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): close round 3 — fence nesting, retry floor, embed budget

- the kept attribute run now has every inner < broken (INNER_LT <\s?
  -> "< ", consuming one ws char keeps it a fixed point) — same-tag
  nesting like <job_posting x=</job_posting> no longer reconstitutes a
  live boundary; cross-tag was already safe (probe-settled); hostile
  set extended with the nested shapes; fenced's bound documented as
  input-cap (+1 char per broken <)
- MIN_RETRY_ATTEMPT_FLOOR 2s: a sub-RTT doomed attempt is refused so
  the actionable 429 outcome is returned, not a generic timeout
- send_embed_with_retry: 3x per-attempt sequence budget restores the
  cold-model-load recovery the total-budget collapse removed (embed
  only; long completion bounds untouched)
- terminal matrix: BOTH (reason, token-cancel) rows now yield
  cancelled (RunTimeout-only would be arbitrary; Budgeted has the
  identical shape); unobservable !token_cancelled term removed from
  timed_out_with_document rather than left mutation-proof
- handoff corrected (15 retry call sites; R8 numbers refreshed)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(renderer): close renderer critic round (10 findings)

- remove now removes: isFabricationResolved requires the verdict and
  the document to AGREE (keep = settled; remove = settled only when
  the span is absent); removeEvidenceLines is line-granular, applied
  through the surface's own editor handler -> debounced commit -> the
  standard save; verdict recorded even when the apply throws; the
  still-present span renders "marked for removal — still in the
  document", never green; badge counts against the LIVE text
- contrast: the five flagged opacity-suffixed sites -> bare remapped
  -400, plus five more of the same shape found in the new code
  (STATUS_TONE bare -300, icon/body -400/80); pre-existing instances
  deferred to a sweep (recorded)
- clean section chips label from the matched document heading (raw
  machine key leaked before); chip test asserts label text
- poll death fixed: undefined-vs-null separated in refetchInterval,
  session hook errors only when no record ever landed (a blip on a
  live run keeps polling); use-resume-pipeline.test.ts (8 tests)
- radio-role cursor exclusion + css guard; pipeline.phase.* i18n en+de;
  resolveError alert test; aria-controls; resolveRunnableDepth wired;
  STORE_VERSION 5 with migration step
- 17/17 mutations caught (4 survivors each produced a better test)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(pipeline): terminal notifications + divergence semantics

- run_notification pure builder (stream.rs truncation precedent) +
  notify_terminal at the one call site with a source lock; four cards
  (completed / needs-review-as-ready / failed / cancelled); unresolved
  count single-sourced via report::unresolved_count with the
  unreviewable-critical branch honest; failed card carries no error
  text (persisted strings can surface as OS banners); backend sends
  strings per the established convention (no rust-side i18n catalog)
- divergence documented structurally: resumeText AND report are
  aggregate-owned, run rows own status/reason/metrics/trail;
  sourceTextHash is the join and hash-stale is the honest state;
  record_decision survives text moves (update_texts never touches
  quality_report — pinned); the Rust merge replaces slots WHOLE (the
  renderer overlay is what preserves fabrications — both directions
  pinned); orphaned fabrications deliberately not reconciled (missing
  evidence IS the success state for a remove verdict)
- 7/7 mutations caught (one false catch recorded honestly: a
  compile-error mutation proves nothing, re-applied as deletion)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(renderer): quality-run entry point on the job detail pane

- TailoredResumePanel sibling to PrepApplicationPanel: DepthSelector +
  small-model warning + run lifecycle + runs list + report, all reused
  as built; fast ROUTES to the existing tailor handler (never
  re-implemented); quality sends the literal depth with no client
  routing/model fields
- traps handled: job.completed mid-run is not done (a busy session
  with a full draft and a running record still renders running);
  nullable stoppedReason; needsReview says "not finished — N claims
  need your verdict"; non-latest runs open read-only with the reason;
  Remove withheld here (no editor for the saved résumé — the verdict
  records and renders marked-for-removal, never claims deletion)
- real defect found+fixed in the session hook: five early-failure
  paths (limiter, completer, doc lookup, job text) fail the umbrella
  job with NO run row — get() answers null and the panel span forever;
  job.failed now consumed while the machine is busy (not while
  record-less — that misses a row stuck at running)
- GeneratingPanel deliberately not imported cross-feature (~25 lines
  of the same primitives; promotion to components/generation recorded)
- default résumé with label (no picker precedent to copy); report
  note field for "not the newest run" / "remove applies in the editor"
- 20/20 mutations caught (3 survivors forced fixture/design fixes)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): notification routes to /jobs where runs now live

The /ai-generate route predated the entry surface; runs start and are
reviewed in the job detail pane's TailoredResumePanel on /jobs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: adr-032 pipeline ownership, adr-033 no model-written memory

Plus domain-model + resume-domain additions for GenerationDepth, the
run store, aggregate-vs-run-owned report semantics, and the
fabrication verdict rule. (Steward wrote these to the main checkout;
relocated to the branch so they ship with the PR.)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(agent): three quality pipeline tools (analyze, report, run)

- tools_pipeline module (tools_quality is at 1213/1400 R8): analyze_job
  (runs the pipeline's own stage struct — shared cache, not a copied
  prompt), get_quality_report (store read, honest hash-stale surface),
  run_quality_pipeline (returns draft+report AS DATA, persists nothing;
  saving stays behind gated save_resume)
- run_quality_pipeline gated to improve_resume_tools (Phase 7), NOT
  prep: the 360s step timeout would kill a 75-min pipeline mid-spend —
  exclusion pinned off the arithmetic, not a name list
- two truncation holes closed: fabrications and draft now shrink
  inside the summary cap instead of being cut mid-JSON by take(cap)
- pre-existing finding pinned honestly: Budget::max_tool_calls has no
  producer anywhere; a naive counter would just trade dead variants —
  documented at the field + a pinning test; real fix (tool suppression
  once spent) needs an AgentEnv signature change, recorded
- AGENT_PREP deliberately NOT resized (the ration is per run, not per
  tool; worst case unchanged at 12 turns / 10 calls)
- 18/18 mutations caught (one initially survived -> source lock added;
  one false claim corrected — the const assert is the guard)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): close the pre-pr ensemble round (2 high + mediums + lows)

- runsForJob invalidated on the session's terminal transition (all
  three ensemble passes converged on this); writable no longer reads
  the possibly-stale list for the session's own run — a just-finished
  run can never be locked read-only with hidden Remove/Keep buttons
- fabrication entries carry the containing LINE (located at report
  build, omitted when absent/blank/>1000 chars — never guessed);
  removeEvidenceLines anchors on exact trimmed-line equality and
  REFUSES without an anchor (executed proof had evidence "250"
  deleting the contact header via substring match); double-Remove race
  closed with an applying gate; line whitelisted OUT of the agent-tool
  summary (measured: including it collapses 20 entries to 6)
- contract completion-signal paragraph rewritten to the settled truth
  (get(runId).status is the authority; job.failed covers pre-row
  failures; stage events are progress-only)
- cursor rule that actually fires: button[aria-disabled=true] in the
  unlayered block (the [role=radio] selector was inert — options are
  buttons); guard test asserts selector + declaration
- notify label clamped to 160 chars (displacement); generatedAt
  coerced numeric-or-null in the tool summary; wire types honest
  (finishedAt/issueCount number|null; criticalCount documented absent
  -not-null); resumePipeline.run job-kind labels en+de; docs: ADR
  index rows, ADR-033 real toolset zero-arg semantics, ADR-032 retry
  claim qualified, ADR-0021 link restored, gitignored-handoff
  reference inlined

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(pipeline): unique remove anchors, document-agreement resolve, regenerate status recompute

review round 1 on #969 (claude workflow), all five findings fixed with
executed mutation evidence:

- containing_line now refuses a span that occurs on more than one line:
  a bare year or figure anchored on whichever line came first in document
  order (an education year instead of the flagged job entry), which is the
  substring failure one level up. uniqueness is text-determined, so
  re-issue determinism is preserved.
- report::unresolved_count/has_unresolved/still_needs_review now take the
  current document texts and apply the renderer's isFabricationResolved
  rule: a recorded remove counts as unfinished until its span leaves the
  document. resolve_fabrication can no longer flip a run to completed
  while the panel still shows a removal pending.
- regenerate_section recomputes the run row status after the wrapper
  write via the shared recomputed_status helper (mirror of resolve's
  clearing arm): a regenerated section that introduces a fresh fabrication
  now moves a completed run back to needsReview.
- the absence arm of factual.altered_project_link (a source link missing
  or altered in the output) no longer enters the remove/keep panel: its
  evidence is by definition not in the document, so the row asked a
  question with no correct answer. it stays a blocking critical, same as
  factual.dropped_role. gate scoped to that one code because
  unsourced_term evidence is normalized and a general presence gate would
  drop genuine entries.
- removeEvidenceLines refuses when the anchor line is duplicated at apply
  time instead of deleting every copy; removalPendingHint now says where
  to finish the edit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: integrate the no-ai-slop catalog into the anti-ai-tell system (#967)

* feat: integrate the no-ai-slop catalog into the anti-ai-tell system

Curates all ~90 catalog items through a four-rule checkability bar (fixed
form, zero factual content, unconditional prompt ban, no hidden domain
meaning): eight high-precision entries join the validated lexical tier
(paramount, transformative, multifaceted, ever-evolving, paradigm shift,
meticulous, widely regarded as, it is worth noting), ~44 items — including
every construction pattern (binary contrasts, colon reveals, fake-profound
kickers, portability test, show-don't-tell) — become prompt guidance the
model is instructed by but user text is never flagged for, and ~19 are
skipped with recorded reasons. Zero structural checks shipped: both
candidates fired on truthful counter-examples ("shipped a status page,
showcasing live latency"; a polite self-answered close) — the family
already removed twice. Words naming real work (utilize, facilitate,
spearhead, beacon) stay validator-invisible by rule, pinned by negative
controls over an ordinary resume; apostrophe-bearing entries are blocked by
a shape test (matching never normalizes punctuation, so they were half-dead
by construction); German stays curated-not-translated with a leak pin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: depth-aware guidance tier and the critic advisories on the tell catalog

The anti-tell blocks split into checked and guidance tiers per depth: brief
ships exactly the lines that back a voice.* check (the validator cannot see
which depth produced the output, so brief may only instruct what it also
verifies), dropping the block share of the small-model letter prompt from
48 to 26 percent; full and task keep the complete text and every other call
site is byte-identical via the depth default. The voice formatting line is
scoped so it no longer contradicts the letter's keyword-bolding output
rules, pinned by a prompt-consistency test. transformative moves to the
prompt tier — it fails the catalog's own no-hidden-domain-meaning rule on
transformative learning and transformative justice, both now negative
controls. Curly apostrophes fold to ascii at the two ai_tell_issues call
sites only (header-name matching untouched), making contraction tells
checkable: it's worth noting, it's important to note and the today's-world
filler join their frequent surface forms — the uncontracted twins needed
their own entries, the for-free hypothesis tested false. Shape guards gain
double-space and leading-non-word checks; the German construction-guidance
asymmetry is recorded as an evidence-driven deferral.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: ensemble findings — depth everywhere, honest tiers, paramount out

The depth tiering reaches all nine prose consumers instead of two:
referral, application-email, rewrite and the interview and answer builders
thread their resolved depth (the last three gained a backward-compatible
target param), roughly halving every small-model system prompt — a brief
referral note drops from 7129 to 4140 chars. The CHECKED constants now
carry only validator-backed phrases: ten prose phrases and nine lexical
strays the module's own tests classify as never-validated moved to the
guidance tier, enforced by a mechanical reverse test that parses the
quoted bans out of the checked lines (a bogus phrase added there now
fails it), shrinking the brief blocks further. paramount moves to the
prompt tier — Paramount Global is a real employer and the exemption reads
only the resume, never the job ad; the employer-name exemption widening is
recorded as a deferral with its injection risk noted (company name, not ad
body). The intermediate-commit baselines are reworded to what main
actually shipped, the budget bound ratchets to a quarter, the opener
matcher folds curly apostrophes like its siblings (with a contraction
opener appended and the load-bearing indices documented), and the vacuous
bold-ban iteration is replaced by unguarded cases per ban-bearing depth.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: coderabbit round-1 findings on the voice-block composition and test rigor

The application-email builder composed its voice block only in the full
branch — brief and task carried no anti-tell rules at all, the format
skeleton's two opener examples being the entire anti-slop surface; the
depth-scoped block is now hoisted into one local composed by all three
branches (full byte-identical), pinned per depth with mutations failing
exactly the branch they remove. The opener tests assert through a
first_evidence Option so a miss names the fixture; the letter negative
control gains the genuinely missing template-opener silence pin while four
comments naming a voice.ai_tell_prose code that never existed are
corrected; the honesty test's normalize folds curly apostrophes like the
matcher it mirrors; and the quoted-ban parser throws loudly on an
unbalanced quote instead of silently shifting every later ban into prose.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: autopilot adopts semantic scoring when enabled (#966)

* feat: autopilot adopts semantic scoring when enabled

Scheduled runs re-rank the keyword prefilter's top survivors through the
same combined kernel as the jobs page — score_one semantics including
languages_align, closing the known divergence on this path — when the user
has semantic scoring on. The webview-only toggle gets a rust-readable
single-column mirror on job_preferences written by settings and boot-sync,
deliberately not a struct field so the full-row set() can never clobber it
(the salary_expectation precedent). Phase two runs after cluster_aware_retain
so minMatchScore keeps its keyword meaning and only deduped survivors cost
an embed, capped at twenty per run from the aggregator's posting cap;
cache ids hash canonical_job_key and the resume text so tracking-param
variants hit the paid row and a resume edit is a miss by construction.
Embed failure degrades that job to keyword-only via an explicit scoreSource
emitted from the same option check as the blend — a run never fails because
of scoring, and the formula version stays unbumped because no score changes.
The autopilot percent label flips to match percent only when semantic is on,
en and de.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: critic blockers on the autopilot semantic re-rank

The translate flag becomes a MatchSurface enum with one shared translates()
table — every surface labelled match percent runs the full jobs-page
pre-processing including translation (the skipped step collapsed coverage
to language-neutral tokens and embedded a cross-lingual cosine, two
different numbers under one label), false only for the extension's
structural zero-egress; pinned by a cross-surface parity test. The
synthetic resume snapshot vector moves out of the shared vectors index into
posting_vectors with its TTL discipline, the write site itself now refuses
synthetic scoring ids (documents/sql.rs split for R8), and a test pins the
index count and stale arithmetic across a semantic run. The tautological
semantic-off test is replaced by should_semantic_rerank plus a phase
function owning the gate, the wall clock (per-run timeout with keyword-only
degrade and a rerank_start step) and a lazy setup closure, so zero-cost-off
is a property of the tested function. Re-ranked head and keyword tail sort
as two blocks; only cluster canonicals are re-ranked (an unreachable
belt-and-braces dedup guard was deleted rather than shipped); daily-cap
charges move inside score() behind an actual-round-trip predicate; the
autopilot locale source now matches the jobs page with detect-and-backfill
recorded as a deferral; mirror-write failures surface a notification.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: charge embeds at the call on the exact bytes and close the advisory gaps

The will-this-reach-the-provider predicate answered a different question
than the call — it hashed the untranslated blob while the embed consumed
translated text (phantom charges on every cache-hit run of a translated
posting) and never saw the resume embed at all (uncharged real embeds,
including after ceiling exhaustion). It is deleted rather than patched:
documents::embed_charged charges at the single choke point all three
embeds pass through, on the miss path only, with a latching per-run budget
that still degrades a refused job to keyword-only. The provider-reaching
effects sit behind a ScoreIo seam so the kernel is testable without an
AppHandle, and the required fixture exists: a translator that actually
rewrites the text, pinning zero charges on a fully-cached translated
posting and exactly one per real embed. score_one also stops caching a
keyword-only number under the semantic key when no embedding backed it —
a refused or provider-offline job no longer freezes the wrong number for
the cache TTL (a pre-existing jobs-page trap). Autopilot delete drops its
orphaned resume vector unless another autopilot shares the text; the
semantic-scoring command returns a real Result so mirror-write failures
reject the promise and the notification can fire; the blob map is
candidate-scoped; import warns-and-skips a synthetic vector row instead of
aborting the restore.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: delta-review findings on the semantic score cache and rerank loop

semantic_available now requires BOTH vectors — a cached posting with a
refused resume embed produced combined = 0.4 x ats labeled combined and
froze it under the semantic cache key for the TTL; both mixed shapes are
pinned as separate tests so the asymmetry that hid this cannot recur, and
the degrade explanation gains a third branch instead of reporting a
similarity that was never measured. The candidate-url set drops its
positional cap (the loop's own counter bounds embeds; the cap silently
cost later jobs their rerank slot when head entries collapsed as URL

head_commit.message:
feat: add jake, awesome and deedy resume templates from the latex classics (#965)

* feat: add jake, awesome, and deedy resume templates

Port three classic LaTeX community resume designs into the Typst engine.
Jake (ATS tier) routes through the parametric single_column.typ with no new
knobs. Awesome and Deedy (design tier) get bespoke .typ files - a thin
accent-tinted header band with accent-bar section markers, and a bold name
block with an accent-colored surname, respectively.

Awesome's white band-text registry field would otherwise leak into the
generic DOCX renderer as invisible white-on-white text, so name_color stays
a real dark ink and the .typ hardcodes white for its own band (mirroring
meridian.typ's existing c-band-text convention). DOCX approximates the band
as run-level shading behind the name run, echoing the Banded cover-letter
layout's flat-shading precedent.

* test: cover jake, awesome, and deedy templates in the golden test matrices

Add the three new templates to canonical_template_ids (every-template PDF
render/extraction/tier tests pick them up automatically), plus dedicated
spec-pin, DOCX-shading, and ATS-mode-honesty tests for Awesome and Deedy.
Sync the frontend picker's tier-badge counts and ATS-toggle gate lists.

Regenerate resume + cover-letter template preview SVGs and the showcase
banner via the offline #[ignore] generators (ran fine on this host in debug
profile). This also refreshes several older templates' previews that had
gone stale since their last regen (a pre-existing gap the generators'
own doc comments already flagged), not just the three new ones.

* chore: regenerate resume + cover-letter template preview assets

New SVGs for jake, awesome, and deedy (resume + cover-letter previews) and
the 16-column showcase banner. Also refreshes academic, atelier, classic,
lebenslauf, meridian, portrait, swiss-minimal, and throughline previews that
had gone stale since their last regen — a pre-existing gap the ignored
generators' own doc comments already flagged, surfaced by running the
required regen for the three new templates.

* docs: sync export templates doc to the sixteen-template set

The doc was stale two PRs deep (still said twelve): cologne-navy from #953
was never added, and this branch adds jake, awesome, and deedy. Counts,
table rows, tier breakdown (nine ats / seven design), and the
parametric-vs-bespoke route note verified against the TemplateId enum and
template constructors in source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: honest ats-mode hint for decorative templates and a shared template id type

The ats toggle hint was a two-way guess (two-column or photo) that predated
design-tier templates with neither trait — awesome and deedy fell to the
photo branch and promised to remove a photo that does not exist. A
PHOTO_TEMPLATE_IDS trait set plus one atsModeHintKey helper now routes all
three cases (two-column, photo, decorative) with new en+de copy, and both
call sites consume the helper so they cannot drift apart again.

templates.ts also stops declaring its own sixteen-literal TemplateId union:
it imports the wire contract's type from @ajh/shared (newly re-exported
through the contracts barrel — it was never in the curated export list), so
a template id added to only one side becomes a tsc error instead of a
silent Classic fallback at deserialization.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: seven export-side review findings on the new templates

jake's name_centered was a render no-op — align(center) inside an
auto-width block; the name, title and contact blocks now take width 100%
when centred (contact included deliberately: the docx path centres all
three off the same flag), pinned by a glyph-geometry test measured from the
rendered svg with a left-aligned control, and the fourteen non-centred
templates verified byte-identical by svg hash. Awesome's docx band becomes
paragraph-level shading with the shared band tint (accent lightened 85%)
and dark ink — the run-level crimson-plus-white approximation contradicted
the banded-letter precedent it cited and hardcoded the invisible-white-text
hazard the registry test guards against — and the band now gates on
ats_mode like its pdf sibling. The suspected band overflow was real but
worse than predicted: the unbounded background layout pushed a long contact
line off the sheet entirely (x=630 on a 595pt page); the header now wraps
inside the printable width and the band grows to 28mm when a title is
present, both pinned by render measurements. deedy's local scale supplement
becomes the section_above_extra registry knob (rule_thickness precedent,
render byte-identical). The validator matrices derive from
canonical_template_ids so a new template cannot skip validator coverage.
Preview assets regenerated (jake, awesome, showcase); export docs and the
stale preview-regeneration note in the knowledge base corrected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: template captions through i18n and a hint test that can actually fail

TEMPLATE_CAPTIONS shipped all sixteen captions as raw English rendered
straight into the template cards; the map now stores translation keys
resolved through t() at the render site, with faithful en and de entries
for every template, pinned by a test using the real translations instance
(it fails on the raw-string map) and a render-level test that fails if the
site skips t(). The atsModeHintKey routing test restated the
implementation's branch order and could not fail; it is replaced by a
design-tier totality check and an overlap invariant — the two-column and
photo sets intentionally intersect on portrait, aria and saffron, so the
suggested disjointness assertion would be false; the overlap is pinned to
exactly those three instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: eight coderabbit findings on the awesome band, theme routing and test rigor

The band's two-line contact budget was confirmed reachable through the real
adapter path — extra_links is an unbounded vec, and twelve of them wrapped a
third line to baseline y=86 against a 79.4pt band bottom, white on white.
band-h is now measured from its own content inside a context (the 24/28mm
thin minimums become floors; descender padding tuned so one and two lines
stay byte-identical), making any line count safe. The duplicated rich-text
ladder collapses to one render-runs-in(runs, link-fill) — and mutating the
band's link fill to the body accent revealed no test pinned it, so the band
region now asserts zero accent-filled glyphs. The docx band decision routes
through theme::has_header_band with droppable-band semantics (meridian also
paints a band but is ats-tier with no toggle; a test pins band templates to
the design tier, and meridian's pre-existing pdf/docx divergence is recorded,
not changed). Tier matrix gains a length-plus-membership guard, awesome's
name color is pinned by equality, and the svg measurement helper now panics
on transforms it cannot parse instead of returning zero — the strict parser
fired on nothing across the engine suite, and the silent zero had been
hiding the link-fill gap above. Docs: route matrix completed to all sixteen,
the copied lightening literal replaced with pointers, and the preview
pipeline documented as its actual two consumers. All rendered svgs verified
byte-identical before and after by hash.

head_commit.message:
feat: add jake, awesome and deedy resume templates from the latex classics (#965)

* feat: add jake, awesome, and deedy resume templates

Port three classic LaTeX community resume designs into the Typst engine.
Jake (ATS tier) routes through the parametric single_column.typ with no new
knobs. Awesome and Deedy (design tier) get bespoke .typ files - a thin
accent-tinted header band with accent-bar section markers, and a bold name
block with an accent-colored surname, respectively.

Awesome's white band-text registry field would otherwise leak into the
generic DOCX renderer as invisible white-on-white text, so name_color stays
a real dark ink and the .typ hardcodes white for its own band (mirroring
meridian.typ's existing c-band-text convention). DOCX approximates the band
as run-level shading behind the name run, echoing the Banded cover-letter
layout's flat-shading precedent.

* test: cover jake, awesome, and deedy templates in the golden test matrices

Add the three new templates to canonical_template_ids (every-template PDF
render/extraction/tier tests pick them up automatically), plus dedicated
spec-pin, DOCX-shading, and ATS-mode-honesty tests for Awesome and Deedy.
Sync the frontend picker's tier-badge counts and ATS-toggle gate lists.

Regenerate resume + cover-letter template preview SVGs and the showcase
banner via the offline #[ignore] generators (ran fine on this host in debug
profile). This also refreshes several older templates' previews that had
gone stale since their last regen (a pre-existing gap the generators'
own doc comments already flagged), not just the three new ones.

* chore: regenerate resume + cover-letter template preview assets

New SVGs for jake, awesome, and deedy (resume + cover-letter previews) and
the 16-column showcase banner. Also refreshes academic, atelier, classic,
lebenslauf, meridian, portrait, swiss-minimal, and throughline previews that
had gone stale since their last regen — a pre-existing gap the ignored
generators' own doc comments already flagged, surfaced by running the
required regen for the three new templates.

* docs: sync export templates doc to the sixteen-template set

The doc was stale two PRs deep (still said twelve): cologne-navy from #953
was never added, and this branch adds jake, awesome, and deedy. Counts,
table rows, tier breakdown (nine ats / seven design), and the
parametric-vs-bespoke route note verified against the TemplateId enum and
template constructors in source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: honest ats-mode hint for decorative templates and a shared template id type

The ats toggle hint was a two-way guess (two-column or photo) that predated
design-tier templates with neither trait — awesome and deedy fell to the
photo branch and promised to remove a photo that does not exist. A
PHOTO_TEMPLATE_IDS trait set plus one atsModeHintKey helper now routes all
three cases (two-column, photo, decorative) with new en+de copy, and both
call sites consume the helper so they cannot drift apart again.

templates.ts also stops declaring its own sixteen-literal TemplateId union:
it imports the wire contract's type from @ajh/shared (newly re-exported
through the contracts barrel — it was never in the curated export list), so
a template id added to only one side becomes a tsc error instead of a
silent Classic fallback at deserialization.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: seven export-side review findings on the new templates

jake's name_centered was a render no-op — align(center) inside an
auto-width block; the name, title and contact blocks now take width 100%
when centred (contact included deliberately: the docx path centres all
three off the same flag), pinned by a glyph-geometry test measured from the
rendered svg with a left-aligned control, and the fourteen non-centred
templates verified byte-identical by svg hash. Awesome's docx band becomes
paragraph-level shading with the shared band tint (accent lightened 85%)
and dark ink — the run-level crimson-plus-white approximation contradicted
the banded-letter precedent it cited and hardcoded the invisible-white-text
hazard the registry test guards against — and the band now gates on
ats_mode like its pdf sibling. The suspected band overflow was real but
worse than predicted: the unbounded background layout pushed a long contact
line off the sheet entirely (x=630 on a 595pt page); the header now wraps
inside the printable width and the band grows to 28mm when a title is
present, both pinned by render measurements. deedy's local scale supplement
becomes the section_above_extra registry knob (rule_thickness precedent,
render byte-identical). The validator matrices derive from
canonical_template_ids so a new template cannot skip validator coverage.
Preview assets regenerated (jake, awesome, showcase); export docs and the
stale preview-regeneration note in the knowledge base corrected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: template captions through i18n and a hint test that can actually fail

TEMPLATE_CAPTIONS shipped all sixteen captions as raw English rendered
straight into the template cards; the map now stores translation keys
resolved through t() at the render site, with faithful en and de entries
for every template, pinned by a test using the real translations instance
(it fails on the raw-string map) and a render-level test that fails if the
site skips t(). The atsModeHintKey routing test restated the
implementation's branch order and could not fail; it is replaced by a
design-tier totality check and an overlap invariant — the two-column and
photo sets intentionally intersect on portrait, aria and saffron, so the
suggested disjointness assertion would be false; the overlap is pinned to
exactly those three instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: eight coderabbit findings on the awesome band, theme routing and test rigor

The band's two-line contact budget was confirmed reachable through the real
adapter path — extra_links is an unbounded vec, and twelve of them wrapped a
third line to baseline y=86 against a 79.4pt band bottom, white on white.
band-h is now measured from its own content inside a context (the 24/28mm
thin minimums become floors; descender padding tuned so one and two lines
stay byte-identical), making any line count safe. The duplicated rich-text
ladder collapses to one render-runs-in(runs, link-fill) — and mutating the
band's link fill to the body accent revealed no test pinned it, so the band
region now asserts zero accent-filled glyphs. The docx band decision routes
through theme::has_header_band with droppable-band semantics (meridian also
paints a band but is ats-tier with no toggle; a test pins band templates to
the design tier, and meridian's pre-existing pdf/docx divergence is recorded,
not changed). Tier matrix gains a length-plus-membership guard, awesome's
name color is pinned by equality, and the svg measurement helper now panics
on transforms it cannot parse instead of returning zero — the strict parser
fired on nothing across the engine suite, and the silent zero had been
hiding the link-fill gap above. Docs: route matrix completed to all sixteen,
the copied lightening literal replaced with pointers, and the preview
pipeline documented as its actual two consumers. All rendered svgs verified
byte-identical before and after by hash.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: native structured output for openai, gemini and ollama with a hardened json parse module (#964)

* refactor(ai-provider): split cursor pagination helpers into pagination.rs

* feat(ai-provider): add complete_structured with a prompt-discipline default

* feat(ai-provider): wire openai response_format json schema

* feat(ai-provider): wire ollama format field for structured output

* feat(ai-provider): wire gemini response schema for structured output

* feat(ai-provider): add anthropic structured-output model gate and correct json-mode capabilities

* feat(pipeline): add pure json extract, repair and typed parse module

* refactor(prompts): drop the unused structured-output profile flag

* refactor(pipeline): compare json delimiters as chars in the balanced scan

* docs: drop the removed structured-output flag from the provider profile description

The branch removed supportsStructuredOutput from ProviderProfile (native
structured output is now decided per-request by the Rust provider layer via
complete_structured); this line still described the old field and behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: harden json extraction and structured-prompt assembly against hostile model output

Security review found the latent complete_structured surface exploitable
before its first caller lands. extract_json committed to the first fenced
block before any deserialization attempt, so a triple-backtick inside a JSON
string value (a job posting with a code fence echoed into a field) hijacked
a fully valid response into all-defaults data reported as success, and an
attacker echoing a fenced object first controlled the parsed value on every
prompt-discipline path. parse now walks ordered candidates — the whole
response when it is exactly one balanced value, then fenced bodies last-first,
then top-level balanced spans last-first — with a clean parse pass for every
candidate before any repair.

JsonParseError derived Debug, re-exposing the exact model content its
hand-written Display withholds ({:?} logging and .expect() panic text reach
the crash reporter); Debug is now hand-written over reason() only. The
re-ask path gets a safe-by-construction reask_detail() that wraps the
fragment in the shared ADR-010 fence with the raw detail() accessor demoted
to pub(crate). structured_prompt now flattens turns through the shared
flatten_messages so assistant/tool provenance markers survive, matches the
system role case-insensitively, and schema translation recursion is
depth-capped, failing whole to the existing fallbacks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: seven pre-pr review findings on the structured-output surface

Containment now overrides the parse pass split: a candidate with a nested
later candidate gets its repair attempt immediately, so a clean fence quoted
inside a container that merely needs repair (raw newline, trailing comma,
smart quotes) can no longer win — while sibling clean-beats-repairable and
the shape-mismatch fallthrough are preserved and now both pinned by tests.
The three native complete_structured overrides thread req.effort through the
same gate as their streaming bodies (openai reasoning_effort, gemini
thinkingLevel without includeThoughts, ollama think), positive and negative
tests each. Both schema translators degrade whole on composition keywords
they cannot walk (anyOf/oneOf/allOf/not/$ref/$defs at any depth) instead of
emitting strict:true over unstrictified subtrees or silently dropping the
constraint. GEMINI_KEPT_KEYWORDS gains the documented value constraints
(pattern, min/max, length and property bounds) verified against the current
Schema reference. The json-only directive no longer references an example on
the empty-hint path, and the public extract_json trap moved into the test
module. Ollama Cloud's response_format delegation is now cited to vendor
docs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: five coderabbit round-1 findings on the structured-output surface

openai_response_format now rides strictify's walk with a doc-verified
OPENAI_STRICT_KEYWORDS allowlist and degrades whole to json_object on any
keyword strict mode does not permit (minLength/minProperties and the
if/then/else family were the real exposure — the finding's pattern example
is stale, pattern is supported now); nothing is ever silently stripped.
contains_version_needle requires component boundaries on both sides of the
needle, rejecting lookalike model ids glued to neighbouring components.
Fence language tags are stripped only when the newline precedes the fence's
own closer and the tag is not JSON punctuation, so a one-line fence no
longer promotes an unrelated span into the fenced tier. bounded's expired
cumulative deadline gets a hermetic regression test, and MAX_CANDIDATES is
pinned (band, bottom-drop truncation, real answer survives).

The sixth finding was disproven: the embed body's embedContentConfig
nesting matches the current v1beta discovery document (rev 20260806), which
marks the top-level outputDimensionality deprecated — the suggested move
would have targeted the deprecated location. Citation recorded in the doc
comment; no code change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: record the gemini embed-body nesting precedent in review-config

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: bound the pathological duplicate-scan test for slow ci runners

The 500ms wall-clock bound held locally but failed all three nextest
retries on the shared CI runner (~2.2s in a debug build), turning every PR
red — including #963 itself at merge time. The assertion's job is to
distinguish the capped scan from an uncapped quadratic blowup (~18M pair
comparisons, tens of seconds anywhere), which a 10s bound still does with
full margin on any runner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: three ai-review round-2 findings on the structured-output surface

The structured path dropped the token limits on every native provider, not
just the reported Ollama: streaming bodies sent num_predict/num_ctx,
max_tokens and maxOutputTokens while the non-streaming builders dropped
them, truncating large resume/job-ad prompts. Each adapter's non-streaming
builder now takes an Option<StructuredCall> mirroring its own streaming
gating field-for-field (absent, never null), with parity tests asserting
against the streaming body's value so the two can only drift together.

The invalid_json_detail re-ask fence tag joins FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS (as a
literal — R7 forbids an agent-from-commands import; the producing side's
test pins the tag text), so a forged parser-detail block inside foreign
fenced content is neutralized like the established tags.

JsonParseError's Syntax/Shape payloads become RawDetail — private field,
content-free Debug, no Display — so pattern matching can no longer reach
raw model text past the content-free formatting; detail() destructures it
pub(crate)-only and reask_detail() stays the public safe path, with a
source-pin guard on the field visibility.

Known pre-existing gap flagged, not half-fixed: the prompt-discipline
fallback still calls the 5-arg complete_with_usage and cannot carry the
limits without a trait change touching every adapter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: two coderabbit round-2 findings on the model gates and strict schemas

The adaptive-thinking gate's bare mythos substring was the last unbounded
needle — claude-notmythos-9 classified adaptive; it now routes through
contains_version_needle, whose component-boundary rule applies unchanged to
a bare family word, keeping family breadth (mythos-6 and later stay
adaptive) pinned by test. Tuple-form and boolean items schemas degrade
whole to json_object: the non-object arm of the strict-keyword walk
returned fine, shipping maxLength and unclosed object members under
strict:true — and the alternative guard placement inside strictify is
provably incomplete (its object arm clones items through untouched).
Gemini's walker already degraded on both tuple shapes; now pinned so the
providers cannot drift.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

head_commit.message:
feat: native structured output for openai, gemini and ollama with a hardened json parse module (#964)

* refactor(ai-provider): split cursor pagination helpers into pagination.rs

* feat(ai-provider): add complete_structured with a prompt-discipline default

* feat(ai-provider): wire openai response_format json schema

* feat(ai-provider): wire ollama format field for structured output

* feat(ai-provider): wire gemini response schema for structured output

* feat(ai-provider): add anthropic structured-output model gate and correct json-mode capabilities

* feat(pipeline): add pure json extract, repair and typed parse module

* refactor(prompts): drop the unused structured-output profile flag

* refactor(pipeline): compare json delimiters as chars in the balanced scan

* docs: drop the removed structured-output flag from the provider profile description

The branch removed supportsStructuredOutput from ProviderProfile (native
structured output is now decided per-request by the Rust provider layer via
complete_structured); this line still described the old field and behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: harden json extraction and structured-prompt assembly against hostile model output

Security review found the latent complete_structured surface exploitable
before its first caller lands. extract_json committed to the first fenced
block before any deserialization attempt, so a triple-backtick inside a JSON
string value (a job posting with a code fence echoed into a field) hijacked
a fully valid response into all-defaults data reported as success, and an
attacker echoing a fenced object first controlled the parsed value on every
prompt-discipline path. parse now walks ordered candidates — the whole
response when it is exactly one balanced value, then fenced bodies last-first,
then top-level balanced spans last-first — with a clean parse pass for every
candidate before any repair.

JsonParseError derived Debug, re-exposing the exact model content its
hand-written Display withholds ({:?} logging and .expect() panic text reach
the crash reporter); Debug is now hand-written over reason() only. The
re-ask path gets a safe-by-construction reask_detail() that wraps the
fragment in the shared ADR-010 fence with the raw detail() accessor demoted
to pub(crate). structured_prompt now flattens turns through the shared
flatten_messages so assistant/tool provenance markers survive, matches the
system role case-insensitively, and schema translation recursion is
depth-capped, failing whole to the existing fallbacks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: seven pre-pr review findings on the structured-output surface

Containment now overrides the parse pass split: a candidate with a nested
later candidate gets its repair attempt immediately, so a clean fence quoted
inside a container that merely needs repair (raw newline, trailing comma,
smart quotes) can no longer win — while sibling clean-beats-repairable and
the shape-mismatch fallthrough are preserved and now both pinned by tests.
The three native complete_structured overrides thread req.effort through the
same gate as their streaming bodies (openai reasoning_effort, gemini
thinkingLevel without includeThoughts, ollama think), positive and negative
tests each. Both schema translators degrade whole on composition keywords
they cannot walk (anyOf/oneOf/allOf/not/$ref/$defs at any depth) instead of
emitting strict:true over unstrictified subtrees or silently dropping the
constraint. GEMINI_KEPT_KEYWORDS gains the documented value constraints
(pattern, min/max, length and property bounds) verified against the current
Schema reference. The json-only directive no longer references an example on
the empty-hint path, and the public extract_json trap moved into the test
module. Ollama Cloud's response_format delegation is now cited to vendor
docs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: five coderabbit round-1 findings on the structured-output surface

openai_response_format now rides strictify's walk with a doc-verified
OPENAI_STRICT_KEYWORDS allowlist and degrades whole to json_object on any
keyword strict mode does not permit (minLength/minProperties and the
if/then/else family were the real exposure — the finding's pattern example
is stale, pattern is supported now); nothing is ever silently stripped.
contains_version_needle requires component boundaries on both sides of the
needle, rejecting lookalike model ids glued to neighbouring components.
Fence language tags are stripped only when the newline precedes the fence's
own closer and the tag is not JSON punctuation, so a one-line fence no
longer promotes an unrelated span into the fenced tier. bounded's expired
cumulative deadline gets a hermetic regression test, and MAX_CANDIDATES is
pinned (band, bottom-drop truncation, real answer survives).

The sixth finding was disproven: the embed body's embedContentConfig
nesting matches the current v1beta discovery document (rev 20260806), which
marks the top-level outputDimensionality deprecated — the suggested move
would have targeted the deprecated location. Citation recorded in the doc
comment; no code change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: record the gemini embed-body nesting precedent in review-config

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: bound the pathological duplicate-scan test for slow ci runners

The 500ms wall-clock bound held locally but failed all three nextest
retries on the shared CI runner (~2.2s in a debug build), turning every PR
red — including #963 itself at merge time. The assertion's job is to
distinguish the capped scan from an uncapped quadratic blowup (~18M pair
comparisons, tens of seconds anywhere), which a 10s bound still does with
full margin on any runner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: three ai-review round-2 findings on the structured-output surface

The structured path dropped the token limits on every native provider, not
just the reported Ollama: streaming bodies sent num_predict/num_ctx,
max_tokens and maxOutputTokens while the non-streaming builders dropped
them, truncating large resume/job-ad prompts. Each adapter's non-streaming
builder now takes an Option<StructuredCall> mirroring its own streaming
gating field-for-field (absent, never null), with parity tests asserting
against the streaming body's value so the two can only drift together.

The invalid_json_detail re-ask fence tag joins FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS (as a
literal — R7 forbids an agent-from-commands import; the producing side's
test pins the tag text), so a forged parser-detail block inside foreign
fenced content is neutralized like the established tags.

JsonParseError's Syntax/Shape payloads become RawDetail — private field,
content-free Debug, no Display — so pattern matching can no longer reach
raw model text past the content-free formatting; detail() destructures it
pub(crate)-only and reask_detail() stays the public safe path, with a
source-pin guard on the field visibility.

Known pre-existing gap flagged, not half-fixed: the prompt-discipline
fallback still calls the 5-arg complete_with_usage and cannot carry the
limits without a trait change touching every adapter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: two coderabbit round-2 findings on the model gates and strict schemas

The adaptive-thinking gate's bare mythos substring was the last unbounded
needle — claude-notmythos-9 classified adaptive; it now routes through
contains_version_needle, whose component-boundary rule applies unchanged to
a bare family word, keeping family breadth (mythos-6 and later stay
adaptive) pinned by test. Tuple-form and boolean items schemas degrade
whole to json_object: the non-object arm of the strict-keyword walk
returned fine, shipping maxLength and unclosed object members under
strict:true — and the alternative guard placement inside strictify is
provably incomplete (its object arm clones items through untouched).
Gemini's walker already degraded on both tuple shapes; now pinned so the
providers cannot drift.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: deterministic content validation and quality report for generated documents (#963)

* feat: add evidence extraction module and move the bullet scorer out of match_resume

rank_trim_candidates' core moves verbatim into documents::evidence::rank_bullets,
which extract_evidence now reuses to structure the source resume into roles,
projects, education and an honest present/absent skill split for one posting.

match_resume keeps a TrimCandidate: From<EvidenceBullet> shim so the
match:trimSuggestions payload is wire-identical (three camelCase fields, score
still a JSON integer) and shrinks 1276 -> 1132 LOC.

keywords_normalized becomes a collect() over the new keywords_normalized_list so
occurrence-counting consumers share one tokenizer instead of forking it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: add deterministic content validators for generated resumes and letters

validate::content checks the text a model wrote against the candidate's own
resume, the posting, and the target language, before anything is rendered. The
rule it mechanically enforces: a model may never produce a Critical - every one
comes from a deterministic comparison against the source document.

24 issue codes in one table (6 Critical, 18 Warning); the constructor reads the
severity from that table so a code and its severity cannot drift. Pure L1 - no
Tauri, no AppHandle, no IO - and one languages_align decision drives every
resume-posting comparison, so a quality report can never contradict the match
score shown for the same pair.

False positives are the risk this module is designed around: every threshold is
a named const with a boundary test, 1900-2099 is excluded from metric checks,
the contact band is skipped, an open-ended source span resolved to a concrete
year is not a fabricated date, and an unusable posting or a wrong-language
output silences the derived comparisons instead of cascading. Three fixtures
assert a clean en resume, a clean de resume and a grounded letter produce
literally zero findings.

lexicon.rs is a hand-stub transcribing the anti-AI-tell lists from
packages/prompts natural-voice.ts; codegen replaces it behind the same
interface. Not implemented: the letter company-name check - ContentInput has no
company field and the frozen code vocabulary has no code for it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: point languages_align at its three real consumers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(prompts): export ai-tell word lists and template openers

Adds AI_TELL_LEXICAL_WORDS_*, AI_TELL_PROSE_WORDS_*, and TEMPLATE_OPENERS_*
arrays to natural-voice.ts as the discrete, codegen-consumable source of
truth behind the prose anti-AI-tell rulesets. The cover-letter prompt's
opener-ban examples now derive from TEMPLATE_OPENERS_EN/DE instead of
separately hand-authored strings, so the prompt bans exactly what the
Rust content validator (generated from these same arrays) checks for.

* feat(validate): generate the content-validator lexicon from prompts

Adds packages/prompts/scripts/gen-prompts-rust.ts (pnpm gen:prompts /
gen:prompts:check, mirroring gen-ipc-rust.ts) and replaces the hand-stubbed
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/validate/content/lexicon.rs with its generated
output, sourced directly from natural-voice.ts's word-list arrays so the
Rust validator can never drift from the prompt's own bans. Moves the
stub's unit tests into content/test.rs (generated files carry no
hand-authored tests) and wires gen:prompts:check into the same CI job
as gen:ipc:check.

* feat(agent): add four résumé-quality read tools to the agent registry

Add validate_resume, search_candidate_evidence, lookup_salary, and
get_trim_suggestions as thin adapters over validate::content,
documents::evidence, and salary_research (zero new business logic).
Split into a sibling agent/tools_quality.rs to stay under the R8
module-size cap, wired into read_tools()/prep_application_tools() via
one call. ToolContext now also carries resume_id so the SOURCE résumé
resolves server-side, never from model-supplied args. Raise
MAX_AGENT_STEPS 12 -> 14 for the two extra optional quality-tool turns
a run may now spend.

* feat(ai-generations): persist quality_report on the application aggregate

Add the deterministic content-quality report as a new column on the
ai_generations aggregate (ADR-007 addendum): additive migration,
AiGenerationRecord field, insert/update/import/row_to_record wiring, and
a pick-non-empty merge rule that also treats the migration's '{}'
placeholder as "no report" so it never clobbers a real one.

* feat(resume): add content-validation ipc command

Expose validate::content::validate_content over ipc as
resume_validate_content: a new zod schema + generated rust request
struct, a server-side-clamped tauri command, and the tauri-client
namespace wiring. Pure/deterministic, no ai call, safe to run on every save.

* feat(ai-generate): add quality-report validation lib and service hook

Renderer-side glue around resume:validateContent: computeQualityReport
(best-effort, never blocks/fails a save), the useValidateContent mutation
hook, and a canned clean-report mock-client stub for tests.

* feat(ai-generate): carry a fresh quality report on every generation save

Both surfaces (AI Generate's useGeneration, TailorFlow's generation-store)
now validate resumeText/coverLetterText right before persisting and attach
the report to the save request; the parsed report lands in session state
(additive report field) and cold-entry hydration seeds it back from a
saved record's qualityReport. Validation failure degrades to a report-less
save, never blocking or failing the generation itself.

* fix(ai-generations): merge quality_report per top-level wrapper key

pick_report treated the whole column as one opaque blob, so a letter-only
save (which only ever carries a coverLetter sub-report) clobbered a stored
resume sub-report and vice versa. Parse both sides as JSON objects and
overlay incoming's top-level keys onto existing's instead, so independent
resume/coverLetter saves layer the same way every other field on this
aggregate already does.

The add_quality_report migration is still unreleased on this branch, so
its default simplifies from '{}' to '' in place (no shipped build has
seen it) and the merge no longer needs a placeholder special case. Also
clamp the save-path quality_report to 256 KB, the same trust-boundary
treatment every other free-text field on this command gets.

* fix(resume): reject an unrecognized doc kind and drop the duplicate span

resume_validate_content silently coerced any unrecognized docKind to
DocKind::Resume and logged the raw request string twice (the command-level
span plus validate_content's own). Reject "resume"/"coverLetter" strictly
with a Validation error, and drop the command-level span entirely — the
inner validate_content span already logs codes/counts (ADR-027).

Add the command-level test coverage this file was missing: oversized
multi-byte inputs and an oversized requirements list are clamped rather
than processed whole (mirrors match_resume's own test), coverLetter
docKind routes to the letter ruleset instead of the résumé-structure
checks, and an unknown docKind is rejected.

* feat(ai-generate): add quality badge, report panel, and hand-edit nudge ui

QualityBadge (self-describing chip, opens QualityReportPanel), the panel
(issues grouped by section, severity chip, guidance-framed message per
issue code with a generic fallback for unknown codes, quoted evidence,
metrics footer), and HandEditNudge (dismissible, once per generation via a
remount key) — wired into both results surfaces. en/de i18n for all new
copy, keyed per issue code (quality.issue.<code>).

* fix(agent): close two fence-boundary forgery gaps in the quality tools

HIGH-1: register the three new agent/tools_quality.rs result tags
(validate_resume_result, search_candidate_evidence_result,
get_trim_suggestions_result) in FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS so a forged tag
smuggled into a job_posting body (or a sibling quality-tool result)
gets neutralized, not just the tag matching its own wrapper.

HIGH-1b: neutralize a forged bare [tool_result:{name}] marker inside
untrusted tool-result bodies before wrapping the real one around it —
FENCE_TAG_PATTERNS only covers the <tag> syntax, not this separate
transcript-boundary format.

Adds regression tests for both, including the critic's probe B (a
job_posting body carrying a forged validate_resume_result block) and
the sibling-tag case.

* fix(validate): stop content validators accusing truthful resumes

Six reproduced false-positive Criticals, each on a document that stated
nothing but the truth:

- project links compare on a canonical key (scheme dropped, host lowered,
  trailing slash removed) and report the verbatim span; a bare host now needs
  a path or a known code host, so a stack line's Socket.IO/Bun.sh no longer
  read as links, and the stack line is excluded structurally as well
- a role survives on any company token of two characters or more, so a
  shortened employer (IBM Deutschland GmbH written as IBM) is not a dropped
  role; legal forms and geography can never be the sole survival evidence
- the language Critical is withheld when the source resume reads as the same
  wrong language, which is detector disagreement rather than a defect, and
  the metrics survive with it
- unsupported_date no longer fires on a later year just because the source
  spelled its open end as seit 2021 / since 2021 / 2021 -, and open-ended
  detection now understands those spellings
- present-tense markers match whole words, so presented, knowledge, currently
  and actually stop reading as date context
- the second-contact-block Critical needs a real address and a name on the
  section's first line, not a bare @ next to any short line

Also: k/m/bn and doubled/2x restatements count as sourced numbers, metric
checks no longer skip every separator-laden body bullet, education entries
with date spans reach the evidence set, German function words are filtered
out of the skills split (locally, never in the scoring kernel's STOPWORDS),
stems never reach a user-facing message, low_coverage needs a five-point
drop, and the report's serialized key set is pinned against its TS mirror.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(validate): stop title_drift matching employers on a shared year

`titled_entries` splits an entry at its FIRST separator, so the date span stays
inside the company string and its year tokens join the company identity set.

* fix(renderer): validate quality_report shape before parsing (m-1)

parseQualityReport cast unknown -> QualityReport with no shape validation,
so a malformed persisted quality_report column crashed the whole app (only
the root ErrorBoundary caught it) every time that record's TailorFlow
opened. Validate schemaVersion + each sub-report's issues array/metrics
object defensively; a malformed sub-report now drops to undefined instead
of throwing, and a malformed issue entry is filtered rather than crashing
the array.

* fix(agent): defeat nested [tool_result] marker forgery in tool results

TOOL_RESULT_MARKER matched a full [tool_result:...] delimited token whose
body admitted a literal `[`, so a forged marker nested inside another one
(e.g. [tool_result:[tool_result:save_resume]]) survived neutralization:
the greedy body stopped at the FIRST `]` (the inner marker's own close),
leaving the fully-formed inner marker untouched in the output.

Match the opening [tool_result PREFIX only and replace with the canonical
"[ tool_result" form, same convention as the fence-tag neutralizer -
every occurrence is found and broken independently of surrounding
brackets, so nesting can no longer hide one marker from the scan.

* perf(validate): cap the near-duplicate bullet scan at 400 bullets

duplicates::validate is an O(bullets²) pairwise Jaccard scan that ran
unbounded — a malformed or hostile "generated" document with thousands of
bullet-shaped lines held a tokio worker for seconds on every save.

Truncate to MAX_DUP_BULLETS (400) before the pairwise pass, mirroring the
count-cap discipline agent::tools_quality already uses. A pathological
bullet count now returns in well under 500ms and still flags a genuine
duplicate placed inside the cap.

* fix(validate): cap the content-report issue list to avoid silent report loss

An uncapped ContentReport.issues could grow the serialized report toward
~1MB on a pathological document (thousands of forged roles / duplicate
bullets). The IPC save path clamps quality_report to 256KB, truncating
that blob mid-JSON; merge_quality_report then fails to parse it and
silently falls back to the OLD stored report — a fresh report just
vanishes.

Cap the issue list at MAX_CONTENT_ISSUES (200) in validate_content itself,
so the byte clamp downstream is never reached. Criticals sort first before
truncation so a warning flood can never push a real Critical out of the
visible list; a trailing REPORT_TRUNCATED marker names the dropped count
instead of a silent cut.

* fix(validate): strip control chars from target-language input

normalize_language only trimmed leading/trailing whitespace before taking
the first 2 characters, so an internal control character (e.g. "a\nb")
survived into the 2-char result. That value reaches this module's own
validate:content span text and content.language_mismatch's evidence — a
log-injection primitive.

Filter to alphanumeric characters before taking the first 2. Also mirror
the Zod targetLanguage.max(32) cap server-side in resume_validate_content,
the same trust-boundary treatment every other field on that command
already gets.

* docs(agent): correct stale four-result-tags comment in the fence-tag registry

The comment claimed four super::tools_quality result tags were registered;
only three are. The fourth tool (lookup_salary) carries no free text to
fence and returns via envelope_result instead. Fix the comment so a future
fenced salary result isn't wrongly assumed already covered.

* fix(ai-generations): clamp quality_report on the bundle import path

The IPC save path already clamps quality_report to QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES
before persisting, but AiGenerationStore::import (a restored backup bundle
- an equally untrusted, user-supplied file) wrote the bundle's quality_report
straight to the column with no cap at all.

Move QUALITY_REPORT_MAX_BYTES into the data layer as the single source of
truth for both write paths, and clamp it in import too.

* docs: point at the content-issue code roster instead of copying its count

* fix(ai-generate): clear stale report before regenerating

handleGenerate cleared resumeOut/coverOut/buffers but never the quality
report, so the 'both'-mode progressive-reveal window (stage done while
the cover still streams) rendered the previous generation's report
against the new resume until persist recomputed one.

* fix(ai-generate): guard recheck against a mid-flight session reset

handleRecheck awaited validateContent.mutateAsync then unconditionally
called onReportChange with a stale closure's report/currentOutput — a
Reset during the in-flight call could re-inject a report into an
already-cleared session. Add an epoch ref bumped whenever meta/
sourceResume/jobAd change, checked before onReportChange fires.

* fix(quality-report): map the truncated-report code and add a message fallback

The synthetic report.truncated code had no i18n key, so it rendered the
generic quality.fallback sentence plus a bare count as evidence. Add
quality.issue.report.truncated (en + de) and make messageFor() fall
back to the Rust-authored issue.message before quality.fallback, so
any future unmapped code degrades to something meaningful.

* fix(validate): key accented project links without a utf-8 boundary panic

canonical_link stripped the scheme with `&s[..8]`, a fixed BYTE offset, so
any project URL whose 7th/8th byte fell inside a multibyte char aborted the
process: `www.café-berlin.de`, `http://éxample.com` and `ab.com/éx` all
panicked with "byte index 8 is not a char boundary". The release profile is
panic = "abort", so the app died mid-generation, before the document was
saved — a German or French project domain was enough to trigger it.

Byte-compare the scheme prefix on `as_bytes()` and only slice once the
prefix is known to be that (pure-ASCII) scheme. Audited the rest of
canonical_link and urls_in: every other boundary already comes from a
char-aware API (`trim`, `trim_end_matches`, `split_once`, regex match
spans), so this was the only fixed-offset cut.

Covered by a canonical_link unit test with a straddling char at each
boundary the function cuts at (2-, 3- and 4-byte widths), the three
reproducer URLs run through the full validate_content path, and an accented
link in the en source/paraphrase fixture pair so the fixture suite carries
it permanently.
